entry.summary: Visa exemption of up to 30 days for tourism. Business, work, speaking and other purposes need the matching visa.
entry.max_stay: 30 days, with a possible one-time extension of up to 30 days from Thai Immigration. Without a justifiable reason, two visa-free entries per calendar year.
entry.pre_arrival: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC), free, within 3 days before arrival, through the Immigration Bureau website or the THIM app. Beware of fake sites that charge.
entry.other: Be ready to show accommodation, enough funds and an onward or return ticket. Get the entry stamp from an immigration officer, never a visa shop.
entry.next_check: Confirm on a Royal Thai Embassy page once one publishes the 30-day list.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host-arranged WP.34 for accepted urgent/ad-hoc work, or Non-B plus work permit
unpaid-speaking.detail: A one-off special academic lecture or seminar may fit the short notification route for up to 15 days, with a possible notified extension.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the Thai host obtain Department of Employment acceptance; use the normal work route for a planned tour.

paid-speaking.detail: The planned paid route is host-led and initially supports a stay of up to 90 days under the visa before longer extensions.
paid-speaking.next: Put the fee, duties, venues and dates into the host's work-permit brief.

book-launch.route: Host-led speaking route; Thai publisher or bookshop handles retail
book-launch.detail: A signing, talk or workshop follows the active-delivery route. Rights and publisher meetings can stay in the business lane.
book-launch.next: Separate the appearance, fee, rights discussion, imports and local book sales.

ai-teaching.route: WP.34 for a genuinely ad-hoc special lecture; Non-B plus work permit for planned or recurring teaching
ai-teaching.detail: Attending technical training is not work, while delivering it is. Education-sector approval may also apply to formal teaching.
ai-teaching.next: Have the university, company or event host choose between urgent notification and the full work route.

remote-work.detail: The DTV is a five-year multiple-entry visa for digital nomads, remote workers and freelancers, with up to 180 days per entry and THB500,000 financial evidence.
remote-work.next: Use it for overseas work; map Thai clients, Thai employment and local paid appearances separately.

entrepreneur.route: Smart S for an established certified Thai startup
entrepreneur.detail: Smart S uses a target-industry startup, director or 25% ownership role and THB600,000 deposit, with no separate work permit for the certified startup.
entrepreneur.next: Test the startup against target-industry certification and company-ownership rules.

trade.route: Meet and negotiate under the visitor/business lane; operate through Non-B, work permission and company approvals
trade.detail: Foreign ownership, company registration and any Foreign Business Licence are separate from personal immigration status.
trade.next: Use the first trip to choose partners and structure, then map the operating role.

artist.route: Non-B plus work permit for planned performance
artist.detail: Thai work guidance expressly addresses foreign singers, artists and influencers. Festival attendance under DTV is not the same as performer permission.
artist.next: Have the promoter sponsor the performance dates, venues, fee and duties.

mixed-mission.route: Enter for the accurate immediate purpose, then let the principal Thai host activate any delivery
mixed-mission.detail: Thailand offers several useful keys: visitor/business attendance, WP.34, Non-B/work permit, DTV and Smart S.
mixed-mission.next: Split the schedule into attendance, delivery, local income, remote work and company operation.

filming.route: Thailand Film Office permission through a registered local coordinator, plus crew work permits
filming.detail: Under the Film Act B.E. 2551 (2008), foreign productions (documentary, music video, commercial, TV) need Thailand Film Office permission, applied for by a coordinator registered with the Office; allow at least 10 working days for script approval. Crew then need work permits; filming on a tourist visa has led to arrests.
filming.next: Engage a registered local coordinator well ahead of the shoot.

research.route: NRCT research permit, then Non-Immigrant RS visa
research.detail: Foreign researchers need NRCT approval at least 90 days before starting, then a Non-Immigrant RS visa.

volunteering.route: Non-Immigrant O (Volunteer) visa plus work permit
volunteering.detail: Even unpaid volunteering needs a Non-Immigrant O visa and a work permit, through a legally registered NGO with a supporting letter from a government department.
volunteering.next: Ask the NGO to start the government letter early.

laws.rule: Severe drug penalties, including the death penalty. Police can demand a urine test; ask to do it at a police station and ask for the Tourist Police (1155). Cannabis is medicinal only, under 0.2% THC by weight and with a locally recognised prescription; using it in public or carrying it out of Thailand is illegal.
laws.penalty_signal: Long jail terms, deportation, death penalty

laws.rule: Australians have been arrested for carrying ADHD, depression and anxiety medicines without the right documents, and for carrying medicine bought at a Thai pharmacy without a prescription. Carry medicines in their original packaging with a copy of the prescription and a doctor's letter naming each medicine, the dose and that it is for personal use.
E-cigarettes, vapes and refills are illegal, even for personal use. Smoking is banned in public areas including beaches, markets and building entrances.
laws.penalty_signal: Importing or selling: up to 10 years' jail or a large fine. Buying or possessing: up to 5 years or a large fine.

laws.rule: Legal age 20. Sale and drinking can be illegal at certain hours, places and days, including religious holidays and voting days.
Carry identification at all times. Making a false statement to police, including about an insurance claim, is illegal. Commercial surrogacy is illegal.
Use an International Driving Permit with your Australian licence for the vehicle type. A motorcycle needs a motorcycle licence, whatever rental companies say. Digital licences may not be accepted.
laws.penalty_signal: Arrest or jail for driving without the right licence

laws.rule: From 15 September 2026 the visa exemption covers tourism only. Overstaying brings a fine before departure and can bring arrest, deportation and a re-entry ban.

items.text: Don’t accept food, drinks or cigarettes from other people.
The death penalty can apply to: murder attempted murder rape drug offences crimes against the state, including treason some offences against the monarchy
Possession of even small quantities of drugs for recreational purposes can lead to long jail sentences and deportation.
Don’t carry drugs for anyone.
Thai authorities may conduct spot-checks for illegal drugs at airports and in tourist areas.
The use of cannabis is limited to medicinal purposes only.
The content of Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) must be below 0.2% in weight and you must have a prescription from a locally recognised professional.

It is illegal to: use cannabis in public places carry cannabis out of Thailand sell cannabis to pregnant and breastfeeding women buy or possess cannabis for those under the age of 20 If you're traveling to or transiting through another destination, drugs, including cannabis, may be illegal there.
The legal age for buying and drinking alcohol is 20 years old.
It may be illegal to buy, sell or consume alcohol at certain times of the day and at certain locations.
E-cigarettes, e-brake, e-cigars, other vaporisers (vapes) and refills are illegal, even for personal use.

Since 23 June 2025, cannabis flower has been a controlled herb. Tourists may not use, buy, carry or transport it without a Thai prescription (Thai traditional medicine, Chinese medicine or dentistry practitioner), which is limited to 30 days' supply. Recreational use is not legal. Online, vending-machine and advertised sales are banned, as are sales at temples, parks and similar public places. Shops openly selling it may be unlicensed.
